finding.claim: Unvalidated icon URL stored by PUT /profile is fetched with a server-side GET by the nightly sync job, enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: Profile.update(String webhook, String icon) parameter icon (Profile.java:11), stored unchecked at Profile.java:16 (this.iconUrl = icon).
finding.sink: HttpClient.send of HttpRequest.newBuilder().uri(URI.create(iconUrl)).GET() in Profile.sync (Profile.java:23-24), using BodyHandlers.ofByteArray().

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives attacker-supplied icon; entry point is PUT /profile (handler not in repo, auth unverified).
Validation applies only to webhook; icon is not checked.
icon stored into this.iconUrl without validation.
Nightly sync(HttpClient c) runs with the server's network position.
URI.create(iconUrl) parses the stored value into a GET request.
Request is sent and the full body is buffered into memory with no size cap; response is discarded, so the SSRF is blind.

finding.guards_checked: icon: no validation. Java HttpRequest only permits http/https schemes (JDK behavior, not run here). No private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking. No IP pinning (not needed, attacker can supply internal IP directly). Redirect policy depends on the caller-supplied HttpClient, which is not visible; default is NEVER. Auth on PUT /profile not visible in repo. webhookUrl (Profile.java:12, sink :21) checked and not a finding: String.matches full-match regex on https://hooks.example.com/[A-Za-z0-9]{20} excludes userinfo, ports, fragments, query, and other hosts; POST body is empty.

verdict.guard_found: none. icon is stored unchecked at src/Profile.java:16 and used directly in URI.create(iconUrl) with GET at src/Profile.java:23-24. The only check is the webhook regex at src/Profile.java:12, which does not cover icon. The redirect policy is set by the caller's HttpClient, which is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace lines at src/Profile.java:11, 12, 16, 20, 23 and 24 all exist and match the claim, and no validation guards icon, so the sink is real and unguarded. But the only entry point is a "// PUT /profile" comment at src/Profile.java:10, with no handler, route, or auth in the repo, so I cannot confirm that a remote low-privilege attacker controls the value passed to update() at src/Profile.java:11.
